original.title: The Cambrian Ocean Has a Hunter — How Deep Do You Hide? 🦐
original.banner: Cambrian hunter: where do you hide?
original.hook_vo: A spiked-claw hunter owns this ocean. Pick a depth.
original.art_direction: Turquoise and sand palette with crisp Cambrian clarity, macro 50mm lens, one warm sunlit amber glint per frame.

options.label: Floating at the surface
options.vo: One: floating at the sunlit surface.
options.image_prompt: view just below a sunlit ocean surface looking up at rippling light, tiny drifting larvae sparkling in turquoise water, one warm amber sun glint dancing on the waves, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

options.label: In the drifting plankton
options.vo: Two: drifting in a plankton cloud.
options.image_prompt: dense shimmering cloud of tiny swimming arthropods and jellies in bright turquoise water, light rays streaming down, one warm golden sun shaft through the swarm, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

options.label: Open water, mid-depth
options.vo: Three: hanging in open water, nowhere to hide.
options.image_prompt: vast empty open water at mid-depth, blue in every direction, a small soft swimming creature alone, a long segmented shadow far off, one warm amber light shaft, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

options.label: Beside the sponge reef
options.vo: Four: beside a reef of cup-shaped sponges.
options.image_prompt: Cambrian reef of tall cup-shaped sponges and branching growths on a sunlit seabed, small shrimp darting between them, one warm amber light patch on the reef crest, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

options.label: Above the trilobite field
options.image_prompt: close view a metre above a seafloor crowded with crawling trilobites, their segmented shells catching light, a big flap-finned predator gliding overhead, one warm amber glint, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

options.label: Flat on the seafloor
options.vo: Six: lying flat on the seafloor mud.
options.image_prompt: POV pressed flat on fine grey Cambrian seafloor mud, trilobites ploughing past at eye level, a huge flap-finned predator silhouette passing high above in bright water, one warm amber glint, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

options.label: Down the reef cliff
options.vo: Seven: dropping down the dark reef cliff.
options.image_prompt: steep underwater cliff of reef rock dropping into deep blue darkness, spiny worms clinging to ledges, one warm amber shaft of light fading along the wall, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

options.label: Lit water, giant eyes
options.vo: Eight: bright open water, facing the clawed hunter.
options.image_prompt: a giant Anomalocaris filling the frame in bright open water, segmented swimming flaps rippling, spiny grasping frontal appendages reaching forward, huge stalked compound eyes, one warm amber sun shaft behind it, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

original.verdict_vo: Real answer: number 6, because this hunter probably avoided the sea bed, where grabbing prey risked claw damage. Lie flat.

fact.text: Anomalocaris probably did not hunt animals on the seafloor, since grabbing prey there at speed could damage its frontal appendages.
fact.source_sentence: It probably would have not hunted benthic animals like trilobites, considering the possibility of damaging the frontal appendages on the substrate while trying to grab prey from seafloor at speed.

original.description: The ocean's first apex predator is cruising overhead and you have eight places to hide. The safest one goes against every instinct.
